Countdown

The countdown is authoritative: the DBSC time shown is the published warning signal. GPS may run beforehand, formal capture begins at T−5:00, and race statistics switch to RACING at 00:00.

Start Line · Ping & Bias

For Hut starts, the Hut end is fixed and only the Pin End is pinged. For committee starts, ping the Committee Boat and Pin End. The line is compared with the active wind direction.

The app projects this device position forward to the estimated bow using the First 31.7 LOA of 9.61 m. Choose the location where the phone/tablet is actually being held when you ping.
Fixed Hut + selected limit mark define the Hut start line. Orange O is the default.
Committee BoatNot pinged
Pin EndNot pinged
Line bearing / length—
Wind—
Device → bow correctionMiddle · +4.81 m
Calculated biasPing both ends

Bias is calculated geometrically from the estimated bow positions at the two pings and the app's current true-wind direction. It does not account for local wind bends, tide at the line, committee-boat movement, GPS error or tactical congestion. Re-ping if the committee boat moves.

Committee start reuses the Committee Boat + Pin End positions from Course Selection. Hut start reuses the fixed Hut and whichever Hut limit mark is selected there.

Finish Location

Ronan & Dean Tools

Boat-performance targets and deeper tide-planning tools.

Boat Polars

A polar describes the boat's predicted target speed at different true wind speeds and true wind angles. Enter your own boat's values; SparklesGPT will use the nearest beat angle in the SailSteer target-tack display instead of the generic 42° fallback.

TWS knBeat TWA °Beat speed knRun TWA °Run speed kn
No boat-specific polar target loaded · fallback beat angle 42°.

Tidal Flow · Rule of Twelfths

Uses the current Dublin Port high/low-water interval to show whether the tide is on the flood or ebb, where you are in the six-part cycle, and a rough relative-flow proxy.

State—
Cycle segment—
Relative flow proxy—
Estimated height—
Previous water—
Next water—

The Rule of Twelfths is a rule-of-thumb for tidal-height change. SparklesGPT uses its 1-2-3-3-2-1 pattern only as a relative current-strength proxy; it is not a measured current speed. Local Dublin Bay direction/strength can differ and should be checked against the tidal atlas and conditions.

Leg type is classified from the angle between course bearing and wind: broadly upwind = BEAT, middle angles = REACH, broadly downwind = RUN.

Summary

Record and finish a race, then run the analysis.

Record this race?

SparklesGPT can record your GPS track so you can review the race afterwards — including tacks, gybes, PORT vs STARBOARD performance, speed, VMG, pointing estimates and manoeuvre losses.

You can still start or stop recording later from the Tracker & Analysis tab.
